title: Made a DAW for remote jamming. Turns out agents can make music in it too.
author: taddeimania
selftext:
My friend and I live in different places and wanted a simple way to pass songs back and forth, so I built a small DAW called Lathe. Along the way I added an MCP connection, mostly so I could ask my assistant things like "why can't I hear the synth on track 2?", or "put in a placeholder drum beat for me to jam over and i'll record drums later". It turned into something more interesting than that.

An agent connected to Lathe can:

* build a whole session: tracks, routing, Lathe's built-in synths, drums and effects (nothing to install), or your own VST3s
* write MIDI parts and set any plug-in's controls by name
* mix and master, export the mix and stems as WAV, and read back the peak and loudness to check its own work

I've been a big fan of watching all of the games from this community for a bit now and I've seen the question about making music come up a number of times. I think this tool might help some people here.

Here's a session step by step: an agent builds a short track, a guitar part gets recorded over it, and the agent mixes and masters it: [https://getlathe.app/ai.html](https://getlathe.app/ai.html)

It's free and open source, on Mac, Windows and Linux. The MCP connection is off by default and only listens on your own machine. It works with Claude, Cursor, VS Code or anything that speaks MCP. The only AI usage built into this app is the one you bring yourself.

I'm curious how you're handling music for your games right now, and what you'd want an agent to be able to do in a DAW. Happy to answer anything.
